name: CloudWatch Logs ingestion/storage → application of the log group
description: Log groups follow <namespace>.<application>[.http_agg|.sys_agg]; wf1 attaches IncomingBytes (ingestion) / storedBytes (storage) shares per group and the owner it resolved from the null applications (metric_owners). Groups nobody owns (/aws/eks/…, /aws/lambda/…, RDSOSMetrics) stay visibly unallocated with their metric_key.

name: CloudWatch custom metrics (EMF) → application by *_agg log bytes
description: MetricStorage:AWS/Logs-EMF is the custom metrics the platform derives from the <namespace>.<application>.http_agg / .sys_agg log groups; each application's share is its *_agg IncomingBytes. Metric stream usage (USE1-CW:MetricStreamUsage) is left to the platform spread until the stream's filter is confirmed to carry only application metrics — flip its usage_type into this rule's scope to attribute it the same way.

name: Security & compliance services → every application (platform cost)
description: AWS Config, GuardDuty, KMS, Inspector, Secrets Manager, Macie: nobody owns them, every application of the account shares them in proportion to the cost it already carries.

name: CloudWatch not attributable by log group → every application (platform cost)
description: Metrics, alarms, dashboards and the log groups nobody owns. Log ingestion/storage buckets carry metric_shares by log group and are handled by the by_metric rule first (lower priority number wins).

name: VPC / networking → every application (platform cost)
description: VPC endpoints, public IPs, NAT: shared network plumbing of the account.
